title: Read a buffer back from the harness
starter:
(* The compiled program prints one line per f32 element: the slot, a space, and
   the 32 bits as 8 hex digits, e.g.  "0 3f800000".  Return the values for slot k,
   in order. Lines may end in \r\n, and blank lines can appear. *)
let read_slot (out : string) (k : int) : float list =
  []
hints: Split the output into lines, split each line on the space, and keep the lines whose slot matches.

`Int32.of_string ("0x" ^ hex)` reads 8 hex digits even when the top bit is set (`0x80000000` becomes `Int32.min_int`), and `Int32.float_of_bits` turns those bits into the float. Don't go through `float_of_string`: the point is to never round anything.
On Windows the lines end in `\r\n`. `String.trim` strips the `\r` and turns blank lines into empty strings, which won't match the `[slot; bits]` pattern.
explain: Printing f32 values as raw bits and rebuilding them with `Int32.float_of_bits` makes the round trip exact: -0.0, NaN, infinities and subnormals all survive, which decimal output with a limited number of digits can't promise. Trimming each line handles CRLF and blank lines, so the same parser works on every platform.
